motivation: Since the age of 6, I've been passionate about computers and software development. My dream? To step to the other side of the screen and create experiences that make users dream. This passion has guided all my decisions and shaped my career toward designing custom websites and applications.
vision: Understanding users' real needs is essential to create solutions that truly reflect them—both functional and intuitive. This human-centered, tailor-made approach is at the heart of every project I take on.
philosophy:
My journey, rich and diverse both academically and professionally, has allowed me to explore many fields and master a wide range of languages and technologies. Today, I'm able to design any type of technical solution — whether it's a website, a mobile app, or more complex systems.
To me, a language or a framework is just one of many ways to bring an idea to life: they're the tools of a digital craftsman. What matters most is deeply understanding the client's needs, maximizing the value of their product, and making it reliable, intuitive, and sustainable. This pragmatic and human-centered vision drives every one of my projects.
pointOne: Identifying the real expectations and key features desired by the end user is the first step in building a relevant and engaging solution.
pointTwo: The nature of the project guides the technical choices: web technologies for a website, mobile tools for an app - Adapting the tech stack to the needs ensures efficiency and consistency.
pointThree: Before reaching a finalized product, it is crucial to design a minimal viable version. It serves as a solid foundation upon which optimizations will gradually be added.
pointFour: Creating an application is exciting, but the ultimate satisfaction lies in its smooth performance during testing. These phases ensure stability and alignment with expectations.
pointFive: Development is a journey of continuous learning. Each project is an opportunity to deepen mastery of technologies and expand expertise.
pointSix: A clear division of tasks, rigorous planning, and smooth communication with clients and collaborators are the pillars of a successful and sustainable project.
contactTips: Curious to get to know me better or learn about my services? Feel free to reach out. Whether you want to chat, ask questions, or simply exchange ideas, you have nothing to lose… except the chance to be pleasantly surprised!

projectTips: Here are some projects I have completed throughout my professional career and personal time. Click on any image to enlarge it and explore the details.
hanoiDescription: During my application for a QML developer position (C++ backend, JavaScript frontend), the company challenged me to demonstrate my skills on a technology I was unfamiliar with. The lead developer set several minimum requirements, including building a functional Tower of Hanoi game with a counter and four disks. Additional optional features were later introduced. Through independent research, I developed an advanced version of the game supporting up to eight disks, drag-and-drop functionality, a challenge mode, a menu, and a victory animation. This project remains one of my proudest achievements and a testament to my ability to quickly learn and deliver high-quality solutions in unfamiliar environments.
werewolfAngularTitle: Werewolves of Miller's Hollow utilities application from One Night/One Crepuscule
werewolfAngularDescription: Back in France, I regularly visited a board game café where I hosted many sessions of the game Werewolf of Thiercelieux. Since we often created new roles to match the original cards, it sometimes became challenging to keep track of everything. To improve this process and explore a new technology, I developed an Angular application that allows role tracking and recording a wide range of information. Later, I successfully adapted this web application into a mobile format using the Capacitor tool.
werewolfKotlinTitle: Werewolves of Miller's Hollow utilities application
werewolfKotlinDescription: I rebuilt this application from scratch using Kotlin to deepen my mobile development skills. This project was essential for my role as a game master at a community board game café I frequented, where I introduced role-playing game culture. My hosts trusted me, and together with friends, we had previously managed sessions using paper. I decided to develop a new version of the app, this time incorporating the original cards, featuring a redesigned interface, improved management of turn order, calls, and information, as well as the ability to create new roles. This is an application I am particularly proud of: lightweight, fast, and intuitive to use.
